title: General Frequency Principle for Linear Approximation Classes
abstract: arXiv:2610.41179v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In this paper, we study a general frequency principle under gradient descent training for the finite linear approximation classes. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the learner amplitude relative to the target amplitude vanishes at high frequencies, uniformly throughout training. We also establish sufficient conditions for low-frequency priority, covering single-frequency targets trained separately and two frequency components trained in the same run. This general frequency principle does not imply that lower frequencies always converge faster. Instead, for two frequencies that satisfy certain comparison conditions, one component will take longer to learn than the other; and in common cases, the longer component has higher frequency. Numerical experiments with Legendre and trigonometric bases validate the theoretical results.

translated_title: 线性逼近类的一般频率原理
translated_abstract: 在本论文中，我们研究了梯度下降训练下有限线性逼近类的一般频率原理。在适当的假设下，我们证明了学习者相对于目标振幅的振幅在高频处趋于零，且在整个训练过程中保持一致。我们还建立了低频优先性的充分条件，涵盖了单独训练的单频目标以及在同一次运行中训练的两个频率分量。这一般频率原理并不意味着低频总是收敛更快。相反，对于满足某些比较条件的两个频率，其中一个分量的学习时间会比另一个更长；并且在常见情况下，学习时间较长的分量具有更高的频率。基于Legendre基和三角基的数值实验验证了理论结果。
tldr: 该论文在梯度下降训练下为有限线性逼近类建立了一般频率原理，证明了高频振幅在整个训练过程中一致衰减至消失，并给出了低频优先性的充分条件，但指出频率越高学习越慢并非绝对规律。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes a general frequency principle for finite linear approximation classes under gradient descent training, proving that learner amplitudes vanish at high frequencies uniformly throughout training and providing sufficient conditions for low-frequency priority, while showing that higher frequencies are not always learned slower.
